meta.title: How it works
meta.description: The full kurtar flow, from discovering a surprise bag to picking it up: why contents aren't known in advance, how late you can cancel, and how pickup windows work.

hero.title: How buying a surprise bag actually works
hero.body: Short version: discover, reserve, pick up during the window. The long version — including the constraints we don't hide — is below.

items.title: 1. Discover bags near you
items.body: The app lists bakeries, pâtisseries, cafés, restaurants, and greengrocers near your location that have published a bag today. You'll see each bag's category, estimated value band, and any diet flags (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, lactose-free) — but not the exact list of items inside.

items.title: 2. Reserve knowing the contents are a surprise
items.body: What ends up in a surprise bag depends on what a business has left over that day, so the exact contents are never guaranteed in advance. What you do know: the category, an approximate value band, an allergen warning, and the price you'll pay. Payment is taken at the moment you reserve.

items.title: 3. Cancel for free up to 2 hours before pickup
items.body: Changed your mind? You can cancel your reservation for a full refund up to 2 hours before the pickup window starts. After that, cancellation isn't possible — because the product is fresh, perishable food, which by law falls outside the general 14-day right of withdrawal (this exception is defined in Turkey's Distance Contracts Regulation and explained again in our pre-contract information form).

items.title: 4. Show up during the pickup window
items.body: Every bag has a specific pickup time window. You cannot collect your bag outside that window — businesses plan their staff and stock around it.

items.title: 5. Show your code, collect your bag
items.body: At the counter, you show the code from the app and staff confirm the handover. It takes seconds and needs no extra device or app.

items.title: 6. Rate it afterwards
items.body: Once you've picked up your bag, you can rate the business and track your own impact (bags rescued, CO2e avoided) from your profile.

receipt.title: Example — bakery bag
receipt.note: Bakery bags typically include bread, simit, and other daily bakery items; exact contents vary by business.

items.title: The contents really are a surprise
items.body: No business commits in advance to exactly what goes into a bag — because what's left at closing time depends on how the day went. You know the category and value band; you don't know the item list.

items.title: The allergen warning is the business's responsibility
items.body: Every bag template carries an allergen warning the business itself writes. If you have a serious allergy, read it before buying and contact the business directly if you need to.

items.title: Missing the pickup window means no refund
items.body: If you don't show up during the pickup window (a no-show), your payment isn't refunded — it's treated like any completed purchase. This is what lets a business set that bag aside for you without being able to sell it to someone else.

meta.title: kurtar for your business — turn end-of-day surplus into revenue
meta.description: You pay nothing if it doesn't sell. A fixed fee per bag, annual membership never charged upfront, payout within 5 business days. Founding-member terms for the first 100 businesses.

hero.title: If it doesn't sell, you don't pay
hero.body: kurtar turns the fresh food you'd otherwise throw away at closing time into revenue. No percentage commission, no upfront fee, no complicated dashboard — just a fixed fee per bag sold.

economics.title: What you earn, what you pay
economics.body: Pricing is a fixed amount per bag sold, not a percentage of your revenue — sell fewer bags and you pay less, sell more and you pay more, but the rate never moves.
economics.bagFeeNote: Charged only on a bag that actually sells. A bag you publish but that doesn't sell costs you nothing.
economics.membershipNote: Never charged upfront. It's offset automatically from your first earnings — "you don't pay before you earn" applies to the membership fee too.
economics.payoutValue: Within 5 business days, at the latest
economics.payoutNote: This isn't a marketing promise — it's a legal obligation under Turkey's e-commerce regulation (ETAHS): funds must reach your account within 5 business days of pickup, at the latest.

receipt.title: Example payout — café bag
receipt.note: Worked example only; the withholding rate and platform fee follow current platform pricing. This example excludes any membership offset or refund clawback.

founding.title: Founding-member terms
founding.body: The first 100 businesses get their first year of membership free, and their per-bag fee locked at a lower rate permanently.
founding.bullet2: Per-bag fee locked at ₺19.00 + VAT (instead of the standard ₺25.00 + VAT)

faq.title: What a shop owner actually asks

items.question: Will this cannibalise my full-price sales?
items.answer: Surprise bags only cover the surplus you'd otherwise throw away that day — you decide when and how many bags to publish. You're never required to put full-price items into a bag; the system doesn't force that.

items.question: How much extra work is it?
items.answer: Once you've set up your bag template, the daily task is just entering that day's quantity and pickup time. At handover, the only step is scanning the customer's code — no extra hardware or training required.

items.question: When do I get paid?
items.answer: Within 5 business days of pickup, at the latest. This is a legal obligation under Turkey's e-commerce regulation (ETAHS) — not a marketing promise, a mandatory deadline.

items.question: What happens if a bag doesn't sell?
items.answer: You pay nothing. The platform fee is only charged on a bag that actually sells and gets picked up.

items.question: When do I pay the membership fee?
items.answer: You never pay it upfront. The annual fee is automatically offset from what you earn selling bags — you don't pay before you earn.

items.question: What changes on the tax side?
items.answer: You still issue the receipt/invoice to the customer yourself (via your cash register or e-Archive), exactly as you do today. The platform separately issues you a commission e-invoice for its own service fee, and withholds 1% from your payout — a mandatory withholding on payments made through intermediary service providers, in effect since 2025.

items.question: Can I sell food past its expiry date?
items.answer: No. Selling food past its use-by date is strictly prohibited, and you commit to this explicitly when you apply. kurtar only covers surplus made that day — still fresh, just unsold.

items.question: What happens if a customer complains?
items.answer: Complaints reach you through your business panel and must be resolved within 15 days by law; kurtar tracks the deadline and steps in if needed.
